_readme: PDF-D11 group-view corpus (pdf-bl-fleet-group-view). ONE entry per state in
app.js's GROUP_VIEW_STATES — the catalogue is the key set, and
__preview__/group-view-scenarios.mjs REFUSES (throws) if this file's keys and
that array disagree in either direction, or if a scenario stops producing the
state it is filed under when run through the SHIPPED groupViewState.
`supports` are /v1/barkparks rows as the fleet payload serializes them
array of GET {main.url}/v1/fleet/roster, whose row shape is fixed by
Barkpark.Tasks.Fleet roster/2: worker, agent, scope, status, capacity,
last_seen, ttl_s, task. `roster: null` means the READ ITSELF never landed.
`now` is the injected clock every scenario is derived against, so the
rendered beat ages are deterministic. It is deliberately LATER than several
rows' last_seen by more than their ttl_s: those rows still carry the status
the SERVER computed, because this console never re-derives offline from an
age. The `working-stale-beat` arm below exists to pin exactly that.

empty.why: A main with no supports at all — the group surface's precondition, not a failure.

roster-conflict.why: Two supports resolve to the SAME roster row: sup-1's slug and sup-9's NAME are both "muscle-1", so the listener identity collides and neither box's status or capacity is attributable.

blocked.why: One support reports the stored `blocked` status. Blocked outranks every healthy signal in the group — a box that needs attention is the thing the operator came for.

offline.why: Both live supports carry the server-computed `offline` status — the STALENESS verdict, made by Barkpark.Tasks.Fleet roster/2 against each row's own ttl_s, not by this page. An order filed now would sit unclaimed.

provisioning.why: No support has reached live yet — both are still coming up, so there is nothing that OUGHT to be beating and calling the group offline would be a slander on a box that was never asked to answer.

cap-hit.why: Every ONLINE support reports slots_free: 0 in the validated capacity object. A legacy free-text capacity carries no number and therefore answers null, never 0 — so a legacy box can never be counted into this state, which is why muscle-3 below is the one that keeps the group out of it in the `working` arm and is absent here.

working.why: The steady state: live supports beating, at least one with room. muscle-3 carries the LEGACY free-text capacity ("1 task") to prove both stored shapes render side by side, and its null slot count keeps it out of the cap-hit tally rather than being read as a fabricated 0.

working-stale-beat.why: THE CRITERION-[1] CONTROL. Byte-for-byte the `working` arm's roster, except muscle-1's last_seen is 47 MINUTES old against its own 120s ttl_s — far past the budget by which roster/2 would have written `offline`. The stored status still says `working`, so a surface that renders the SERVER's staleness verdict says working, and a surface that grew a second deriver off last_seen says offline. The pin asserts working.

roster-unreachable.why: The roster READ never landed (roster: null). presenceChip answers the honest "No heartbeat yet" for every support rather than a fabricated Offline, and because unknown is not online the group reads offline — an operator is told the truth about what can be claimed, not about the boxes.
